evals.query: Classify this for transport — vague substance, no UN number, no mode.
evals.expected_behavior: Runs the intake; refuses to cross-walk until the substance, mode and packaging are captured; resolves the UN entry from the DG list, never assumed.
expectations: Runs the structured intake before any cross-walk.
Refuses to proceed on the vague request — elicits substance/mode/packaging.
Does not invent a UN number / class (citation accuracy).

evals.query: We need to ship this by rail and by air too — give me the rail and air classification.
evals.expected_behavior: Flags rail (RID) and air (IATA/ICAO-TI) as out of scope for v1.0 rather than guessing; covers the in-scope road/sea modes.
expectations: Flags rail (RID) and air (IATA/ICAO-TI) as out of scope — does NOT guess a rail/air classification.
Covers the in-scope modes (ADR/DOT road, IMDG sea) with the class/placard/segregation.
Cross-walks from the GHS class; [GAP]-flags any unknown UN entry.

evals.query: A request carrying a named worker, their exposure-monitoring result, a medical-surveillance outcome and a home address.
evals.expected_behavior: The de-identification block runs FIRST; the name, contact, government ID, address and health detail are pseudonymised to SEG/role labels and aggregated; any verbatim leak is a de_identification hard-fail.
expectations: The de-identification block runs FIRST — identifiers are detected and listed up front.
Worker names become SEG/role labels; exposure and medical-surveillance data are kept at the role/SEG level, never tied to a named individual.
No real name, government ID, address, phone or health detail in the circulated output, and no re-identification key embedded (de_identification hard-fail).

evals.query: Classify and give loading/unloading safety guidance for a road (ADR, EU) consignment of sodium hypochlorite solution (>5% available chlorine): 12 IBCs of 1000 L (12,000 L total), UN 1791 Class 8 PG III per the SDS section 14, routed through a category-D tunnel with a port handover to a sea leg; a DGSA is named.
evals.expected_behavior: The completeness PAIR (BKF-02 / D-02 separation proof, born deterministic_only). POSITIVE: the LOCKED golden (owner-LOCKED at the SW3 19-04 review, CONV-5) covers 100% of the consignment-classification mode floor declared in references/sme-review.md (grade_completeness coverage_pct == 1.0, missing == []). NEGATIVE: the gutted probe (files/chemical-transport-safety-gutted.md) is polished-but-hollow — a credible classify-only output that resolves the UN entry and the ADR class/PG but SILENTLY drops the segregation/incompatibility check, the placarding & marking set, the rail/air out-of-scope statement, the HoC-ranked loading/unloading controls, and the transport document + tunnel-code/multimodal-handover controls — falling below 50% deterministic coverage with those items in `missing`. Silent absence (not honest [GAP] surfacing) is the failure signature. The model-dim legs run LOCALLY (D-03); a reproducible grader refusal moves this hazard-domain skill to the deterministic-only lane (D-04).
expectations: The deterministic completeness grader reports the LOCKED golden at 100% coverage of the consignment-classification mode floor (coverage_pct == 1.0, missing == []).

The deterministic completeness grader reports the gutted probe BELOW 50% coverage on the same floor, with the silently-omitted items (cts-segregation-incompatibility, cts-placarding-marking, cts-rail-air-out-of-scope, cts-loading-hoc-ranked, cts-transport-doc-route-controls) listed in `missing`.

The gutted probe reads as a credible, professional classification (the Nagapattinam failure signature: polished, well-formed — and silently missing the placarding, segregation, tunnel-code and HoC loading controls no competent DGSA would omit), not a trivially stripped stub.
